ges_home.featured_title: Carbonation of cement-based materials from a Whole Building Life Cycle Assessment perspective
ges_home.featured_desc: This study develops a structured framework for integrating concrete and mortar CO₂ uptake into Whole Building Life Cycle Assessment (WBLCA), combining the Possan and Collins carbonation models. Applied to a Brazilian social housing case study and assessed against EN 16757 and Monte Carlo simulations, results show that mortars carbonate rapidly during use, while concrete contributes predominantly after demolition. Combined CO₂ uptake offsets 32–38% of cementitious material impacts and 13–16% of total production emissions.

home.title: Welcome to the ASCENC Project
home.description: ASCENC (Sustainability Assessment in Cities and Buildings in New Climates) aims to research the interactions between cities, buildings, and future climates to reduce the environmental impact of civil construction and adapt the urban context to ensure habitability and resilience.

about.title: About the ASCENC Project
about.p1: The ASCENC project – Sustainability Assessment in Cities and Buildings under New Climates – emerged from the combination of Igor Catão Martins Vaz's doctoral thesis with Professor Enedir Ghisi's research project. ASCENC is part of the research project "Sustainability assessment of buildings and urban centers", submitted to CNPq under the CNPq/MCTI Call No. 10/2023, coordinated by Enedir Ghisi. As a differential, it includes articles from Igor Catão Martins Vaz's thesis, which addresses the impact of climate change on the environmental assessment of the built environment.
about.p2: The project organizes its publications and tools into six integrated thematic axes. Each axis focuses on a set of methods, data, and applications in cities and buildings under current and future climates:
about.axis1_desc: Outdoor and indoor thermal comfort, urban heat islands, future climate files (morphed EPWs), metrics such as UTCI/PMV, and strategies for thermal conditioning and urban design.
about.axis2_desc: Precipitation indices (RX1day, RX5day, SDII, R20mm, CDD, CWD, R95p, PRCPTOT, SI), analysis of historical and future patterns, flood risks, and applications in urban and agricultural planning.
about.axis3_desc: Potential and sizing of rainwater harvesting systems (RWH), water performance under future climate scenarios, and economic and environmental analysis of residential and urban systems.
about.axis4_desc: Benchmarking and simulation of systems (electric shower, gas, electric boiler, solar with backup), INMETRO/INI-R parameterization, primary energy, and sensitivity to habits and future climate.
about.axis5_desc: Quantification of CO₂ absorption by carbonation in concrete and mortars, A1–5 boundaries and service-life scenarios, with implications for GHG inventories.
about.axis6_desc: LCA of materials, systems, and buildings; integration with local and global databases (e.g., Ecoinvent, SIDAC), boundary definition, environmental indicators, and comparative studies.

tools.title: ASCENC Tools
tools.intro: The ASCENC tools are interactive dashboards developed to support researchers, designers and managers in assessing the impact of climate change on the built environment. Each dashboard explores a specific thematic axis of the project, based on global climate models and Brazilian context data.
tools.desc_paimt: Interprets future climate conditions in Brazilian cities for thermal comfort and energy efficiency analysis.
tools.desc_paimp: Evaluates future precipitation indices to support decisions in urban drainage and water resource planning.
tools.desc_paimaa: Estimates electricity consumption for water heating under different climate scenarios and usage patterns.
tools.desc_paimrwh: Assesses the impact of climate change on rainwater harvesting systems in Brazilian single-family homes.
tools.desc_paimacv: Will integrate life cycle assessment with future climate scenarios. Under development.
tools.desc_paicacv: Quantifies CO₂ absorption by carbonation in cementitious materials throughout the building life cycle.

paimt.title: Climate Change Impact Assessment Panel - Thermodynamics
paimt.description: PAIM-T is a tool developed to interpret future climate conditions in Brazilian cities. The main objective is to provide researchers, policymakers, and professionals with a comprehensive platform to assess and mitigate the impacts of climate change, offering accurate data for thermal comfort and energy efficiency modeling. For more details, access it directly on Zenodo.

paimp.title: Climate Change Impact Assessment Panel - Precipitation
paimp.description: PAIM-P is a panel developed to interpret future precipitation patterns in Brazilian cities, based on data from the CLIMBra project and 19 global climate models. The tool offers precipitation indices such as RX1day, RX5day, SDII, R20mm, CDD, CWD, R95p, PRCPTOT, and SI, allowing for detailed analyses on urban drainage, flood risks, agricultural planning, rainwater harvesting, and other applications. The panel is free, open-access, and designed to facilitate decision-making in public policies and urban planning, helping to build more resilient environments in the face of climate change. For more details, access it directly on the Zenodo repository.

paimaa.title: Climate Change Impact Assessment Panel - Water Heating
paimaa.description: PAIM-AA is a tool developed to support the assessment and optimisation of water heating in households. The tool assesses electricity consumption for water heating in different climate scenarios and provides key indicators and metrics to help decision-makers assess and respond quickly to climate-related challenges. Designers can compare electricity consumption in electric showers in different cities, modify user behaviour patterns, and assess the impact of future climate change. More details can be obtained from the dashboard or by analysing the parquet database available in the Zenodo repository.

paicacv.title: Carbonation and CO₂ Sequestration Calculator for Buildings (PAIC-ACV)
paicacv.description: PAIC-ACV is a tool dedicated to quantifying CO₂ absorption through carbonation in cement-based materials (concrete and mortar), integrating service life and end-of-life (EoL) scenarios. The platform enables analyses from a Whole Building Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) perspective, assisting in the estimation of the net balance of emissions and carbon sequestration over time.

paimrwh.title: Climate Change Impact Assessment Panel - Rainwater Harvesting
paimrwh.description: PAIM-RWH presents the projected impacts of climate change on rainwater harvesting systems across 652 Brazilian cities. By combining multi-model climate projections with a daily water balance model, it evaluates the potential for potable water savings and system reliability in single-family houses under historical conditions and future scenarios (SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5). Explore how regional variations in rainfall and climate projections affect rainwater harvesting performance, providing uncertainty-aware insights for climate-informed system design.

ges_research.line6: Climate change and the built environment
ges_research.line8: Rational use of water in buildings
ges_research.project1_title: Sustainability assessment of buildings and urban centers
ges_research.project1_desc: This research investigates the environmental, social, and economic impact of sustainable interventions in the built environment through Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). The main objective is to model the synergy of sustainable decisions at the building level and analyze their integrated benefits on an urban scale.
ges_research.project2_title: Urban Green Infrastructure for Safe Greywater Treatment and Reuse
ges_research.project2_desc: The project aims to enhance urban water circularity through decentralized green infrastructure solutions for non-conventional water management. It develops a spatially explicit City Information Model (CIM) and dynamic IoT-based monitoring and control systems to optimize greywater treatment and rainwater reuse.
ges_research.project3_title: Soluções sustentáveis para melhorar a segurança hídrica de cidades localizadas em Santa Catarina
ges_research.project3_desc: O projeto visa identificar soluções sustentáveis para melhorar a segurança hídrica em cidades de Santa Catarina, com foco no uso de telhados verdes e pavimentos permeáveis para filtragem e aproveitamento de água de chuva em edificações.

netuno.title: Netuno
netuno.transition_title: Meet Triton — The Official Successor to Netuno
netuno.transition_desc: Modernized computational platform featuring Brasil (BRL), Ibérica (IBE), and International (INT) editions, integrating continuous simulation, engineering economics, LCA, and MCDA.
netuno.description_full: Netuno is UFSC's pioneering software for estimating potable water savings potential in residential and commercial buildings through rainwater harvesting. It applies daily simulation with historical precipitation records for tank sizing and technical-economic feasibility assessment across non-potable uses (toilet flushing, irrigation, cleaning, and evaporative cooling).
netuno.authors: Prof. Enedir Ghisi and Eng. Marcelo Marcel Cordova
netuno.setup_desc: Official installer for Microsoft Windows (compatible with Windows 7, 8, 10, and 11). Includes executable and guided wizard in Portuguese.
netuno.manual_desc: Complete technical reference manual (June/2014 edition). Details mass balance equations, input data setup, and graphical interpretation.
netuno.support_desc: Formatted rainfall time-series and sample case study data to directly reproduce the exercises illustrated in the user manual.
netuno.install_step1: Extract the SetupNetuno4_ptbr.zip archive to a local folder.
netuno.install_step2: Run Setup.exe and follow the Portuguese installation wizard.
netuno.install_step3: Consult the PDF Manual to format the rainfall time-series for your target location.
netuno.legacy_box_desc: Versions 1, 2, and 3 (2000s to 2013) were originally implemented in Excel/VBA spreadsheets by Prof. Enedir Ghisi and the UFSC team. They formed the foundational algorithms for rainwater harvesting in Brazil, subsequently consolidated into Netuno 4 and now succeeded by Triton.

projects.title: Research Projects
projects.subtitle: Discover our ongoing and completed research initiatives
projects.ascenc_subtitle: Sustainability Assessment of Buildings and Urban Centers
projects.ascenc_desc: The project investigates the environmental, social, and economic impacts of sustainable interventions in the built environment under climate change and new social dynamics such as remote work. It uses Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methodology to compare buildings with sustainability measures against traditional construction models in the country. The goal is to model the integration of individual building solutions at the urban scale, optimizing synergies to foster more resilient cities.
projects.green4grey_subtitle: Urban Green Infrastructure for Safe Greywater Treatment and Reuse
projects.green4grey_desc: The project aims to enhance urban water circularity through decentralized green infrastructure solutions for non-conventional water management. It develops a spatially explicit City Information Model (CIM) and dynamic IoT-based monitoring and control systems to optimize greywater treatment and rainwater reuse. By integrating nature-based solutions with risk assessment frameworks, the study addresses environmental and health compliance across diverse urban and climatic pilot contexts.
projects.rainwater4all_subtitle: Sustainable solutions to improve water security in cities located in Santa Catarina
projects.rainwater4all_desc: The project aims to identify sustainable solutions to improve water security in cities in Santa Catarina, focusing on the use of green roofs and permeable pavements for filtering and harvesting rainwater in buildings. The research covers state-of-the-art reviews on nature-based solutions (NbS), computer simulations to assess the impacts of climate change on water supply, and tests with physical models of permeable pavements.
projects.climate_adaptation_title: Climate Adaptation and Rational Use of Water in Buildings
projects.climate_adaptation_desc: This research evaluates thermo-energetic performance and water and energy end-uses in residential, commercial, and public buildings in Brazil. Through computer simulations and material testing, it aims to establish design guidelines tailored to different Brazilian bioclimatic zones. The findings support the development of technical standards for sustainability, energy efficiency, and water conservation.
projects.completed_1_title: Thermal Comfort and User Behaviour in Shared Workspaces in a Subtropical Climate
projects.completed_1_subtitle: Human dimension of energy consumption and IoT monitoring
projects.completed_1_desc: The study evaluated the influence of the human dimension on energy consumption in hybrid-ventilated offices in a subtropical climate. Thermal comfort questionnaires and IoT devices were deployed to monitor user interactions with air conditioning, windows, and lighting. The collected data enabled the creation of computer simulation models that better reflect occupant behavior in shared corporate environments.
projects.completed_2_title: Thermal Comfort in Commercial Buildings with Hybrid Ventilation in a Subtropical Climate
projects.completed_2_subtitle: Experimental and subjective comfort evaluation methods
projects.completed_2_desc: The project developed a method to evaluate thermal comfort in commercial buildings alternating between natural ventilation and mechanical cooling. It performed microclimate measurements alongside perception questionnaires and experimental metabolism assessments. The research contributed to establishing thermal acceptability criteria and supporting national databases on hybrid-ventilated buildings.

triton_papers.title: Scientific Papers: From Netuno to Triton
triton_papers.subtitle: Over 20 years of pioneering research and empirical validation in rainwater harvesting developed by the Sustainable Space Research Group at the Federal University of Santa Catarina (UFSC).
triton_papers.banner_title: Evolution of Computational Tools in the Group:
triton_papers.banner_line1_text: All scientific publications developed to date by the group on rainwater harvesting simulation and tank sizing utilized the pioneering Netuno software (versions 1, 2, 3, and 4).
triton_papers.banner_line2_text: The new computational platform Triton is the successor software under active development in the group (featuring LCA, water tariff structures, and MCDA). No previous paper used Triton yet; future research and publications from 2026/2027 onward will utilize the Triton platform.
